Authentication flow (OIDC authorization code + PKCE)

Rendered as source: no static drawing is bundled for this diagram.

Mermaid source
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Browser
    participant W as webapp
    participant K as Keycloak
    U->>W: GET /login
    W->>W: generate state, nonce, code_verifier
    W-->>U: 302 /auth?code_challenge=S256(verifier)&state
    U->>K: GET /auth (front channel)
    K-->>U: login form (theme demo)
    U->>K: POST credentials
    K->>K: policies: brute-force, password, required actions
    K-->>U: 302 /callback?code&state
    U->>W: GET /callback
    W->>K: POST /token (code, code_verifier, client_secret) [back channel]
    K-->>W: access, ID and refresh tokens
    W->>W: validate ID token (nonce, issuer, signature), start session
    W-->>U: 302 /profile + session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure online)

Logout is RP-initiated: /logout clears the local session and redirects to Keycloak's end_session_endpoint with id_token_hint, ending the SSO session; Keycloak returns to WEBAPP_PUBLIC_URL/.

Authorization model

Two layers cooperate:

  1. Identity roles and groups - employees grants realm role app-user; managers grants app-admin (composite, includes app-user). They appear in the token as realm_access.roles and groups.
  2. Keycloak Authorization Services on client demo-api - the API never hard-codes who may do what. It asks Keycloak for a decision on resource#scope; Keycloak evaluates the policies in the realm.

Service-to-service flow (client credentials)

Rendered as source: no static drawing is bundled for this diagram.

Mermaid source
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as service client (demo-service)
    participant K as Keycloak
    participant A as api
    S->>K: POST /token grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret
    K-->>S: access token (sub = service account, role app-service, aud demo-api)
    S->>A: GET /api/service/data (Bearer token)
    A->>A: verify signature, issuer, audience, expiry
    A->>K: UMA decision service-data#read
    K-->>A: true (service-policy)
    A-->>S: 200

No user and no browser are involved; the same API code path and the same policy engine decide, which is why the service account gets 403 on /api/reports and /api/admin.

Log dashboard

Rendered as source: no static drawing is bundled for this diagram.

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
    R[request] --> BR["before_request: start timer"]
    BR --> H[route handler]
    H --> AR["after_request: HTTP_REQUEST<br/>method, path, status, duration"]
    H -->|"callback / logout / refresh"| AU["LOGIN, LOGOUT, TOKEN_REFRESH,<br/>TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING, ACCESS_DENIED"]
    H -->|"api-call, s2s"| AP["API_CALL, S2S_REQUEST"]
    AR --> S[("logapp.app_events")]
    AU --> S
    AP --> S
    AU --> US[("user_sessions / audit_log")]
    KE["Keycloak /admin/realms/demo/events<br/>(service account, view-events)"] -->|"sync every N s, dedupe_key"| S
    S --> D["/dashboard and /events.json<br/>filters + pagination"]
    S --> ST["/admin statistics"]
  • Two sources, one table. source=app rows are written by the Flask hooks; source=keycloak rows come from the events REST endpoint (LOGIN, LOGIN_ERROR, REFRESH_TOKEN, CODE_TO_TOKEN, CLIENT_LOGIN, ...). A content hash (dedupe_key) makes re-reading overlapping windows idempotent.
  • Authorization. Any realm user may sign in and sees only their own rows (the username filter is pinned); the realm role app-admin sees everything and the admin panel. Denied attempts are logged as ACCESS_DENIED.
  • Token lifecycle. Before each request the token is checked: with fewer than LOGAPP_EXPIRY_WARN_SECONDS left a TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING is logged and the refresh token is used (TOKEN_REFRESH). A failed refresh is logged as TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED; the session ends (TOKEN_EXPIRED) only when the access token has really expired.
  • Token handling and PostgreSQL. Access, ID and refresh tokens are kept only in the process memory (TokenVault, keyed by an opaque session id). The browser cookie holds the session id and a few claims, and PostgreSQL never receives token material: user_sessions stores username, roles, timestamps and the end reason only.
  • Admin API access. Keycloak 26.8 requires the audience <host>/admin/realms/<realm> on Admin REST tokens, supplied by the optional scope kc-admin-api. The service account holds only view-events.
PostgreSQL event flow
Mermaid source
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant L as logapp
    participant K as Keycloak
    participant P as PostgreSQL
    U->>K: login, token refresh, logout
    K->>P: INSERT public.event_entity (only types in enabledEventTypes)
    U->>L: request
    L->>P: INSERT logapp.app_events (source=app)
    loop every LOGAPP_SYNC_INTERVAL seconds
        L->>K: GET /admin/realms/demo/events?dateFrom=...&first=...&max=200 (Bearer, scope kc-admin-api)
        K-->>L: JSON events
        L->>P: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING (source=keycloak)
        L->>P: UPDATE sync_state keycloak_events_watermark_ms
    end

Keycloak does not store REFRESH_TOKEN events by default. The realm therefore lists 25 enabledEventTypes explicitly (keycloak/realm/demo-realm.json), including REFRESH_TOKEN, LOGOUT, CODE_TO_TOKEN and CLIENT_LOGIN. The TOKEN_REFRESH rows of the application and the REFRESH_TOKEN rows of Keycloak are two views of the same operation and are kept apart by the source column.

Network and URL design

Browsers and containers reach Keycloak by different names, which is the classic Keycloak container pitfall:

Actor Address used Why
Browser KC_HOSTNAME (http://localhost:8080 or https://auth.example.com) Public front channel; defines the token issuer
webapp, api, logapp (back channel) http://keycloak:8080 (logapp: token, refresh and /admin/realms/<realm>/events) Container-to-container, no TLS round trip through the proxy
Token validation in the API OIDC_ISSUER = KC_HOSTNAME/realms/<realm> The issuer is the public one, even though keys are fetched internally

KC_HOSTNAME_BACKCHANNEL_DYNAMIC=true lets Keycloak answer internal requests with endpoints derived from the request host, while front-channel URLs and the iss claim stay on KC_HOSTNAME.

Configuration as code

  • keycloak/realm/demo-realm.json is baked into the image (/opt/keycloak/data/import) and imported with --import-realm on first start. ${PLACEHOLDER} values are resolved from the container environment, so the repository contains no secrets.
  • The build stage of keycloak/Dockerfile runs kc.sh build once, so the runtime starts with --optimized (faster start, fixed DB vendor, health and metrics enabled).
  • The theme keycloak/themes/demo extends the built-in keycloak.v2 login theme with one stylesheet.

Security decisions

Topic Decision
Browser client Confidential client, code flow + PKCE S256, exact redirect URI, implicit and password grants off
Service client Client credentials only, least-privilege role app-service, secret from .env, token cached in memory
Tokens Access token 5 min. webapp: tokens are inside the signed (not encrypted) HttpOnly Flask cookie, never in browser storage. logapp: tokens only in server memory, the cookie holds an opaque session id
CSRF State/nonce on login; per-session CSRF token on every POST to the API proxy route; SameSite=Lax cookies
API Signature + issuer + audience + required claims; algorithm allow-list rejects none; authorization delegated to Keycloak policies; fail closed (deny on error)
Audience Audience mapper adds demo-api so a token minted for another API is not accepted
Credentials Brute-force detection, password policy, passwords and secrets only via .env (random, mode 600, git-ignored)
Containers Non-root users, multi-stage builds, pinned tags, ports bound to 127.0.0.1, management port 9000 not published
Transport Online: Caddy terminates TLS, HSTS, nosniff, referrer policy, optional admin allow-list
Log dashboard data Usernames and IP addresses are stored in logapp; non-admins see only their own rows (filter pinned server-side); the sync account holds view-events only; retention is the operator's job (see Deployment)
Known demo trade-offs Self-registration, demo-cli password grant and fixed demo users exist for convenience; each can be switched off (see Deployment hardening)

Testing strategy

Level Tooling Scope
Unit pytest (213 tests) Log dashboard (store, event sync, token lifecycle, filters, access control, verification script), token validation (expiry, issuer, audience, forged and alg=none tokens), policy client, API endpoints with a fake policy point, web app flows with a stubbed Authlib client, service client token caching, helpers
Configuration pytest Realm file consistency (policy/resource/scope references), no clear-text secrets, every compose variable documented, every realm placeholder passed to Keycloak, Dockerfile policy
End to end scripts/verify.sh Runs against the live stack, local or online: discovery, JWKS, PKCE, 401/403/200/201 matrix with real user and service tokens, then verify_logapp.py (scripted browser session on the dashboard)

logapp/log_app.py - 406 lines, extracted from the repository at build time

"""Log dashboard: an OpenID Connect client for Keycloak that records and displays what happens around it.

What is logged (all into the ``logapp`` schema, see ``store.py``):
  * auth events of this app        LOGIN, LOGIN_FAILED, LOGOUT, ACCESS_DENIED
  * token lifecycle                TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING, TOKEN_REFRESH, TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED, TOKEN_EXPIRED
  * HTTP access of this app        HTTP_REQUEST (method, path, status, duration)
  * calls to the demo API          API_CALL (with the user's token)
  * service-to-service calls       S2S_REQUEST / S2S_ERROR (client credentials of ``demo-service``)
  * Keycloak's own event log       LOGIN, LOGIN_ERROR, LOGOUT, REFRESH_TOKEN, CLIENT_LOGIN ... (see event_sync.py)

Tokens never reach the browser or the database: they live in an in-process vault keyed by an opaque session id,
so the app runs with ONE gunicorn worker (threads) and users sign in again after a restart.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import secrets
import threading
import time
from functools import wraps

import requests
from authlib.integrations.flask_client import OAuth
from flask import (Flask, abort, flash, g, jsonify, redirect, render_template, request, session,
                   url_for)
from werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix import ProxyFix

from event_sync import KeycloakEventSync
from log_config import Config
from log_helpers import (DAY_MS, build_logout_url, decode_jwt_payload, fmt_day, fmt_ts, page_count,
                         page_number, parse_filters, realm_roles, seconds_left, severity)
from store import Store
from token_source import TokenSource

log = logging.getLogger("logapp")

API_CALLS = {  # key -> (method, path, label)
    "me": ("GET", "/api/me", "Who am I?"),
    "reports": ("GET", "/api/reports", "Read reports (app-user)"),
    "admin": ("GET", "/api/admin", "Admin panel (app-admin)"),
}
ADMIN_API_SCOPE = "kc-admin-api"  # Keycloak 26.8+: adds the Admin REST API audience to the token
RANGES = {"1d": 1, "7d": 7, "30d": 30}
NO_LIFECYCLE = {"static", "healthz", "login", "callback", "logout"}
EVENT_KINDS = ("auth", "access", "token", "api", "s2s")


class TokenVault:
    """Server-side token storage keyed by session id (never serialised, never sent to the browser)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._data: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def put(self, sid: str, entry: dict) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._data[sid] = entry

    def get(self, sid: str | None) -> dict | None:
        with self._lock:
            return self._data.get(sid) if sid else None

    def pop(self, sid: str | None) -> dict | None:
        with self._lock:
            return self._data.pop(sid, None) if sid else None


def create_app(config: Config, store: Store, oauth: OAuth | None = None, http=requests,
               s2s_tokens: TokenSource | None = None, sync: KeycloakEventSync | None = None,
               clock=time.time) -> Flask:
    """Application factory; ``oauth``, ``http``, ``s2s_tokens``, ``sync`` and ``clock`` can be injected in tests."""
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.update(SECRET_KEY=config.session_secret, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME="logapp_session",
                      SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="Lax",
                      SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=config.secure_cookies)
    if config.trust_proxy:
        app.wsgi_app = ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_for=1, x_proto=1, x_host=1)

    if oauth is None:
        oauth = OAuth(app)
        oauth.register(name="keycloak", client_id=config.client_id, client_secret=config.client_secret,
                       server_metadata_url=config.discovery_url,
                       client_kwargs={"scope": "openid profile email", "code_challenge_method": "S256"})
    kc = oauth.keycloak
    vault = TokenVault()
    s2s = s2s_tokens or TokenSource(config.token_url, config.service_client_id, config.service_client_secret, http)
    app.extensions["logapp"] = {"store": store, "vault": vault, "sync": sync, "s2s": s2s}

    def now_ms() -> int:
        return int(clock() * 1000)

    def record(event_type: str, kind: str, **fields) -> None:
        """Store an event; logging must never break a request."""
        try:
            store.add_event(event_type=event_type, kind=kind, ts=now_ms(), **fields)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("could not store event %s", event_type)

    def elapsed_ms(started: float) -> int:
        return int((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)

    def is_admin() -> bool:
        return config.admin_role in session.get("roles", [])

    # ---- token lifecycle ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def refresh_tokens(sid: str, entry: dict, reason: str) -> bool:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        who = dict(username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"))
        try:
            if not entry.get("refresh_token"):
                raise RuntimeError("no refresh token")
            resp = http.post(kc.load_server_metadata()["token_endpoint"], timeout=10,
                             data={"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": entry["refresh_token"],
                                   "client_id": config.client_id, "client_secret": config.client_secret})
            resp.raise_for_status()
            tok = resp.json()
            new_claims = decode_jwt_payload(tok["access_token"])
        except Exception as exc:
            record("TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED", "token", error=str(exc)[:200], duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started),
                   detail={"reason": reason}, **who)
            return False
        entry.update(access_token=tok["access_token"], id_token=tok.get("id_token", entry.get("id_token")),
                     refresh_token=tok.get("refresh_token", entry["refresh_token"]))
        exp = new_claims.get("exp")
        store.touch_session(sid, now_ms(), access_expires_at=int(exp * 1000) if exp else None, refreshed=True)
        record("TOKEN_REFRESH", "token", duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started),
               detail={"reason": reason, "expires_in": seconds_left(exp, clock())}, **who)
        return True

    def end_local_session(sid: str | None, reason: str) -> None:
        vault.pop(sid)
        if sid:
            store.end_session(sid, now_ms(), reason)
        session.clear()

    def enforce_token_lifecycle(sid: str):
        """Warn before the access token expires, refresh it, and end the session when that is impossible."""
        entry = vault.get(sid)
        if entry is None:  # process restarted: the server-side tokens are gone
            end_local_session(sid, "server_restart")
            return None
        store.touch_session(sid, now_ms())
        exp = decode_jwt_payload(entry["access_token"]).get("exp")
        left = seconds_left(exp, clock())
        if left > config.expiry_warn:
            return None
        if entry.get("warned_exp") != exp:  # one warning per access token
            entry["warned_exp"] = exp
            record("TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING", "token", username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"),
                   detail={"seconds_left": left})
        if refresh_tokens(sid, entry, "auto") or left > 0:
            return None
        record("TOKEN_EXPIRED", "token", username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"))
        end_local_session(sid, "token_expired")
        flash("Your session expired. Please sign in again.", "error")
        return redirect(url_for("index"))

    # ---- request hooks: access log ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    @app.before_request
    def begin():
        g.started = time.perf_counter()
        sid = session.get("sid")
        if sid and request.endpoint not in NO_LIFECYCLE:
            return enforce_token_lifecycle(sid)
        return None

    @app.after_request
    def access_log(resp):
        if request.endpoint not in ("static", "healthz"):
            record("HTTP_REQUEST", "access", username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"),
                   method=request.method, path=request.path, status=resp.status_code,
                   duration_ms=elapsed_ms(g.get("started", time.perf_counter())), ip=request.remote_addr)
        return resp

    @app.context_processor
    def inject():
        return {"user": session.get("user"), "admin": is_admin(), "csrf": session.get("csrf"),
                "client_id": config.client_id}

    app.jinja_env.filters.update(ts=fmt_ts, day=fmt_day)
    app.jinja_env.globals["severity"] = severity

    # ---- access control ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def login_required(fn):
        @wraps(fn)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            if not session.get("sid"):
                return redirect(url_for("login"))
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper

    def admin_required(fn):
        @wraps(fn)
        @login_required
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            if not is_admin():
                store.audit(session.get("user"), f"{request.method} {request.path}", "denied", ip=request.remote_addr,
                            now=now_ms())
                record("ACCESS_DENIED", "auth", username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"),
                       path=request.path, error=f"requires realm role {config.admin_role}")
                abort(403, f"This page needs the realm role {config.admin_role}.")
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper

    def check_csrf():
        if request.form.get("csrf") != session.get("csrf"):
            abort(400, "invalid CSRF token")

    @app.errorhandler(400)
    @app.errorhandler(403)
    @app.errorhandler(404)
    def http_error(exc):
        return render_template("error.html", code=exc.code, message=exc.description), exc.code

    # ---- authentication routes --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @app.get("/")
    def index():
        if session.get("sid"):
            return redirect(url_for("dashboard"))
        return render_template("index.html")

    @app.get("/login")
    def login():
        return kc.authorize_redirect(f"{config.public_url}/callback")

    @app.get("/callback")
    def callback():
        try:
            token = kc.authorize_access_token()
        except Exception as exc:  # state mismatch, denied consent, bad code ...
            log.warning("login failed: %s", exc)
            record("LOGIN_FAILED", "auth", error=str(exc)[:200], ip=request.remote_addr)
            flash("Login failed. Please try again.", "error")
            return redirect(url_for("index"))
        claims = token.get("userinfo") or {}
        access = decode_jwt_payload(token["access_token"])
        username = claims.get("preferred_username") or access.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("sub")
        roles = realm_roles(access)
        ksid = access.get("sid") or access.get("session_state")
        if session.get("sid"):
            end_local_session(session["sid"], "replaced")
        sid = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        session.clear()
        vault.put(sid, {"access_token": token["access_token"], "id_token": token.get("id_token"),
                        "refresh_token": token.get("refresh_token")})
        session.update(sid=sid, user=username, name=claims.get("name") or username, roles=roles, ksid=ksid,
                       csrf=secrets.token_urlsafe(16))
        exp = access.get("exp")
        store.start_session(sid, username=username, user_id=claims.get("sub"), kc_session_id=ksid, roles=roles,
                            ip=request.remote_addr, access_expires_at=int(exp * 1000) if exp else None,
                            now=now_ms())
        record("LOGIN", "auth", username=username, user_id=claims.get("sub"), session_id=ksid,
               client_id=config.client_id, ip=request.remote_addr, detail={"roles": roles})
        return redirect(url_for("dashboard"))

    @app.get("/logout")
    def logout():
        sid, ksid, name = session.get("sid"), session.get("ksid"), session.get("user")
        entry = vault.get(sid) or {}
        id_token = entry.get("id_token")
        if sid:
            record("LOGOUT", "auth", username=name, session_id=ksid, client_id=config.client_id,
                   ip=request.remote_addr)
            end_local_session(sid, "logout")
        try:
            end_session = kc.load_server_metadata()["end_session_endpoint"]
        except Exception:  # identity provider unreachable: still logged out locally
            return redirect(url_for("index"))
        return redirect(build_logout_url(end_session, id_token, f"{config.public_url}/", config.client_id))

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz():
        ok = store.ping()
        return jsonify(status="UP" if ok else "DOWN", database=ok), (200 if ok else 503)

    # ---- dashboard --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def current_filters() -> dict:
        """Admins may filter freely; everybody else is pinned to their own username."""
        return parse_filters(request.args, force_username=None if is_admin() else session.get("user"))

    @app.get("/dashboard")
    @login_required
    def dashboard():
        filters = current_filters()
        page = page_number(request.args)
        rows, total = store.query_events(filters, page, config.page_size)
        entry = vault.get(session["sid"]) or {}
        exp = decode_jwt_payload(entry.get("access_token", "")).get("exp")
        form = {k: request.args.get(k, "") for k in ("username", "event_type", "kind", "source", "status", "q",
                                                      "date_from", "date_to")}
        return render_template("dashboard.html", rows=rows, total=total, page=page,
                               pages=page_count(total, config.page_size), form=form,
                               event_types=store.event_types(), kinds=EVENT_KINDS,
                               live=request.args.get("live") == "1", api_calls=API_CALLS,
                               expires_in=seconds_left(exp, clock()), api_result=session.pop("api_result", None),
                               sync_error=(sync.last_error if sync else None),
                               args={k: v for k, v in request.args.items() if k != "page"})

    @app.get("/events.json")
    @login_required
    def events_json():
        """Same filters as the dashboard, as JSON (polling clients, scripts/verify.sh)."""
        rows, total = store.query_events(current_filters(), page_number(request.args), config.page_size)
        return jsonify(total=total, page=page_number(request.args), page_size=config.page_size, events=rows)

    @app.post("/api-call/<key>")
    @login_required
    def api_call(key):
        check_csrf()
        if key not in API_CALLS:
            abort(404)
        method, path, label = API_CALLS[key]
        entry = vault.get(session["sid"]) or {}
        started, status, body = time.perf_counter(), 0, {}
        try:
            resp = http.request(method, config.api_base_url + path, timeout=10,
                                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {entry.get('access_token', '')}"})
            status = resp.status_code
            try:
                body = resp.json()
            except ValueError:
                body = {"raw": resp.text[:300]}
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            body = {"error": f"API unreachable: {exc}"}
        record("API_CALL", "api", username=session.get("user"), session_id=session.get("ksid"), method=method,
               path=path, status=status or None, duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started), client_id="demo-api",
               error=None if 0 < status < 400 else body.get("message") or body.get("error"))
        session["api_result"] = {"label": label, "request": f"{method} {path}", "status": status, "body": body}
        return redirect(url_for("dashboard"))

    @app.post("/s2s")
    @login_required
    def s2s_call():
        """Service-to-service probe: this app acts as ``demo-service`` (client credentials) towards the API."""
        check_csrf()
        path, started, status, body, error = "/api/service/data", time.perf_counter(), 0, {}, None
        try:
            resp = http.get(config.api_base_url + path, timeout=10,
                            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {s2s.token()}"})
            status = resp.status_code
            body = resp.json() if resp.content else {}
            if status == 401:
                s2s.invalidate()
            if status >= 400:
                error = body.get("message") or body.get("error")
        except (requests.RequestException, ValueError) as exc:
            error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:200]
        record("S2S_REQUEST" if status and status < 400 else "S2S_ERROR", "s2s", username=f"service-account-{config.service_client_id}",
               client_id=config.service_client_id, method="GET", path=path, status=status or None,
               duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started), error=error, detail={"triggered_by": session.get("user")})
        session["api_result"] = {"label": "Service-to-service (client credentials)", "request": f"GET {path}",
                                 "status": status, "body": body or {"error": error}}
        return redirect(url_for("dashboard"))

    # ---- admin panel ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @app.get("/admin")
    @admin_required
    def admin():
        range_key = request.args.get("range") if request.args.get("range") in RANGES else "7d"
        days = RANGES[range_key]
        now = now_ms()
        stats = store.stats(now - days * DAY_MS, now, config.idle_minutes * 60_000, days=max(days, 7))
        peak = max([d["logins"] + d["failed"] for d in stats["daily"]] + [1])
        store.audit(session.get("user"), "view admin panel", "ok", ip=request.remote_addr, now=now)
        return render_template("admin.html", stats=stats, range_key=range_key, ranges=list(RANGES), peak=peak,
                               sessions=store.recent_sessions(10), audit=store.recent_audit(10), sync=sync,
                               now=now)

    @app.post("/admin/sync")
    @admin_required
    def admin_sync():
        check_csrf()
        added = sync.run_safely() if sync else 0
        store.audit(session.get("user"), "sync keycloak events", "ok" if not (sync and sync.last_error) else "error",
                    target=f"{added} new", ip=request.remote_addr, now=now_ms())
        flash(f"Keycloak event sync finished: {added} new event(s)." if not (sync and sync.last_error)
              else f"Sync failed: {sync.last_error}", "error" if sync and sync.last_error else "info")
        return redirect(url_for("admin"))

    return app


def build(env=None) -> Flask:
    """Wire the production objects: config -> store -> Keycloak event sync (background thread) -> Flask app."""
    env = os.environ if env is None else env
    config = Config.from_env(env)
    store = Store(config.database_url)
    store.init_schema()
    # Event sync authenticates as the service account of the log app's own client (realm role view-events).
    sync = KeycloakEventSync(store, TokenSource(config.token_url, config.client_id, config.client_secret,
                                          scope=ADMIN_API_SCOPE),
                             config.admin_api_base, interval=config.sync_interval)
    app = create_app(config, store, sync=sync)
    sync.start()
    return app


def get_wsgi_app() -> Flask:  # gunicorn entry point: ``log_app:get_wsgi_app()``
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    return build()


if __name__ == "__main__":  # local development server only
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    build().run(host=os.environ.get("LOGAPP_HOST", "127.0.0.1"), port=int(os.environ.get("LOGAPP_PORT", "8083")))

"""Persistence layer of the log dashboard: PostgreSQL in the stack, SQLite for tests and quick local runs.

All timestamps are stored as epoch milliseconds (BIGINT), the same unit Keycloak uses for ``event_time``,
so no time zone conversions are needed in SQL. SQL is written once with ``?`` placeholders and translated
for psycopg (``%s``).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any, Iterator

DAY_MS = 86_400_000

_COLUMNS = ("ts", "source", "kind", "event_type", "username", "user_id", "client_id", "session_id", "ip",
            "method", "path", "status", "duration_ms", "error", "detail", "dedupe_key")


def _ddl(postgres: bool) -> list[str]:
    pk = "BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY" if postgres else "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT"
    return [
        # Every observable event: HTTP access, auth, token lifecycle, service-to-service, Keycloak events.
        f"""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_events (
            id {pk}, ts BIGINT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
            username TEXT, user_id TEXT, client_id TEXT, session_id TEXT, ip TEXT,
            method TEXT, path TEXT, status INTEGER, duration_ms INTEGER, error TEXT, detail TEXT,
            dedupe_key TEXT UNIQUE)""",
        "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_events_ts ON app_events (ts)",
        "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_events_type ON app_events (event_type)",
        "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_events_user ON app_events (username)",
        # One row per login of this application (token material is NOT stored here).
        """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_sessions (
            sid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT, user_id TEXT, kc_session_id TEXT, roles TEXT, ip TEXT,
            login_at BIGINT NOT NULL, last_seen_at BIGINT NOT NULL, access_expires_at BIGINT,
            refreshes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, logout_at BIGINT, end_reason TEXT)""",
        "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_sessions_user ON user_sessions (username)",
        # Who looked at / did what in the admin area of this application.
        f"""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
            id {pk}, ts BIGINT NOT NULL, actor TEXT, action TEXT NOT NULL, target TEXT, ip TEXT,
            outcome TEXT NOT NULL)""",
        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_state (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)",
    ]


def dedupe_key(*parts: Any) -> str:
    """Stable identity of an upstream event: a hash of its content, independent of Keycloak's own event id."""
    return hashlib.sha256("|".join("" if p is None else str(p) for p in parts).encode()).hexdigest()[:40]


class Store:
    """Thin DB-API wrapper. ``url`` is ``postgresql://...`` or ``sqlite:///relative.db`` / ``sqlite:///:memory:``."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, schema: str = "logapp"):
        self.postgres = url.startswith(("postgresql:", "postgres:"))
        self.url, self.schema = url, schema
        self._memory = None
        self._memory_lock = threading.RLock()  # the single in-memory connection is shared by all threads
        if not self.postgres:
            # SQLAlchemy convention: sqlite:///rel.db, sqlite:////abs/path.db, sqlite:///:memory:
            path = url[len("sqlite://"):][1:] if url.startswith("sqlite://") else url
            self.path = ":memory:" if path in ("", ":memory:") else path
            if self.path == ":memory:":  # one shared connection, otherwise every connect() is a new DB
                self._memory = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)

    # ---- connection handling -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @contextmanager
    def _conn(self) -> Iterator[Any]:
        if self.postgres:
            import psycopg
            conn = psycopg.connect(self.url, connect_timeout=5, options=f"-csearch_path={self.schema}")
        else:
            conn = self._memory or sqlite3.connect(self.path, timeout=10)
        lock = self._memory_lock if conn is self._memory else None
        if lock:
            lock.acquire()
        try:
            yield conn
            conn.commit()
        except Exception:
            conn.rollback()
            raise
        finally:
            if lock:
                lock.release()
            else:
                conn.close()

    def _sql(self, sql: str) -> str:
        return sql.replace("?", "%s") if self.postgres else sql

    def _exec(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> None:
        with self._conn() as c:
            c.execute(self._sql(sql), params)

    def _all(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[dict]:
        with self._conn() as c:
            cur = c.execute(self._sql(sql), params)
            names = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return [dict(zip(names, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]

    def _one(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> Any:
        rows = self._all(sql, params)
        return next(iter(rows[0].values())) if rows else None

    def init_schema(self) -> None:
        if self.postgres:
            import psycopg
            with psycopg.connect(self.url, connect_timeout=5, autocommit=True) as c:
                c.execute(f'CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "{self.schema}"')
        for stmt in _ddl(self.postgres):
            self._exec(stmt)

    def ping(self) -> bool:
        try:
            return self._one("SELECT 1") == 1
        except Exception:
            return False

    # ---- events --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def add_event(self, *, event_type: str, kind: str, source: str = "app", ts: int | None = None,
                  detail: dict | None = None, **fields: Any) -> bool:
        """Insert one event; returns False when an event with the same ``dedupe_key`` already exists."""
        unknown = set(fields) - set(_COLUMNS)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown event fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
        row = {c: None for c in _COLUMNS}
        row.update(fields, ts=ts if ts is not None else int(time.time() * 1000), source=source, kind=kind,
                   event_type=event_type, detail=json.dumps(detail, sort_keys=True) if detail else None)
        cols = ", ".join(_COLUMNS)
        marks = ", ".join("?" for _ in _COLUMNS)
        with self._conn() as c:
            cur = c.execute(self._sql(f"INSERT INTO app_events ({cols}) VALUES ({marks}) "
                                      "ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING"),
                            tuple(row[k] for k in _COLUMNS))
            return cur.rowcount == 1

    @staticmethod
    def _where(f: dict) -> tuple[str, list]:
        clauses, params = [], []
        if f.get("username_exact"):
            clauses.append("username = ?")
            params.append(f["username_exact"])
        if f.get("username"):
            clauses.append("LOWER(username) LIKE ?")
            params.append(f"%{f['username'].lower()}%")
        for column in ("event_type", "kind", "source"):
            if f.get(column):
                clauses.append(f"{column} = ?")
                params.append(f[column])
        if f.get("date_from") is not None:
            clauses.append("ts >= ?")
            params.append(int(f["date_from"]))
        if f.get("date_to") is not None:
            clauses.append("ts < ?")
            params.append(int(f["date_to"]))
        status = f.get("status")
        if status:  # "404" exact, "4xx" class
            if len(status) == 3 and status[1:].lower() == "xx" and status[0].isdigit():
                clauses.append("status >= ? AND status < ?")
                params += [int(status[0]) * 100, int(status[0]) * 100 + 100]
            elif status.isdigit():
                clauses.append("status = ?")
                params.append(int(status))
        if f.get("q"):
            clauses.append("(LOWER(COALESCE(path,'')) LIKE ? OR LOWER(COALESCE(error,'')) LIKE ?)")
            params += [f"%{f['q'].lower()}%"] * 2
        return (" WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)) if clauses else "", params

    def query_events(self, filters: dict, page: int = 1, page_size: int = 25) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
        where, params = self._where(filters)
        total = self._one(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM app_events{where}", tuple(params)) or 0
        page = max(1, page)
        rows = self._all(f"SELECT * FROM app_events{where} ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
                         tuple(params) + (page_size, (page - 1) * page_size))
        return rows, int(total)

    def event_types(self) -> list[str]:
        return [r["event_type"] for r in self._all("SELECT DISTINCT event_type FROM app_events ORDER BY 1")]

    # ---- sessions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def start_session(self, sid: str, *, username: str, user_id: str | None, kc_session_id: str | None,
                      roles: list[str], ip: str | None, access_expires_at: int | None, now: int) -> None:
        self._exec("INSERT INTO user_sessions (sid, username, user_id, kc_session_id, roles, ip, login_at, "
                   "last_seen_at, access_expires_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                   (sid, username, user_id, kc_session_id, ",".join(roles), ip, now, now, access_expires_at))

    def touch_session(self, sid: str, now: int, access_expires_at: int | None = None,
                      refreshed: bool = False) -> None:
        self._exec("UPDATE user_sessions SET last_seen_at = ?, access_expires_at = COALESCE(?, access_expires_at), "
                   "refreshes = refreshes + ? WHERE sid = ? AND logout_at IS NULL",
                   (now, access_expires_at, 1 if refreshed else 0, sid))

    def end_session(self, sid: str, now: int, reason: str) -> None:
        self._exec("UPDATE user_sessions SET logout_at = ?, end_reason = ? WHERE sid = ? AND logout_at IS NULL",
                   (now, reason, sid))

    def get_session(self, sid: str) -> dict | None:
        rows = self._all("SELECT * FROM user_sessions WHERE sid = ?", (sid,))
        return rows[0] if rows else None

    def username_for_user_id(self, user_id: str) -> str | None:
        return self._one("SELECT username FROM app_events WHERE user_id = ? AND username IS NOT NULL "
                         "ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1", (user_id,))

    def recent_sessions(self, limit: int = 10) -> list[dict]:
        return self._all("SELECT * FROM user_sessions ORDER BY login_at DESC LIMIT ?", (limit,))

    # ---- audit log -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def audit(self, actor: str | None, action: str, outcome: str, target: str | None = None,
              ip: str | None = None, now: int | None = None) -> None:
        self._exec("INSERT INTO audit_log (ts, actor, action, target, ip, outcome) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                   (now if now is not None else int(time.time() * 1000), actor, action, target, ip, outcome))

    def recent_audit(self, limit: int = 15) -> list[dict]:
        return self._all("SELECT * FROM audit_log ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?", (limit,))

    # ---- sync state ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def get_state(self, name: str, default: str | None = None) -> str | None:
        value = self._one("SELECT value FROM sync_state WHERE name = ?", (name,))
        return default if value is None else value

    def set_state(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
        self._exec("INSERT INTO sync_state (name, value) VALUES (?, ?) "
                   "ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value", (name, value))

    # ---- statistics ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def stats(self, since_ms: int, now_ms: int, idle_ms: int, days: int = 7) -> dict:
        def count(extra: str) -> int:
            return int(self._one(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM app_events WHERE ts >= ? AND {extra}", (since_ms,)) or 0)

        kc = "source = 'keycloak'"
        top = self._all("SELECT username, COUNT(*) AS logins FROM app_events WHERE ts >= ? AND source = 'keycloak' "
                        "AND event_type = 'LOGIN' AND username IS NOT NULL GROUP BY username "
                        "ORDER BY logins DESC, username LIMIT 5", (since_ms,))
        http = self._all("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(duration_ms) AS avg_ms, "
                         "SUM(CASE WHEN status >= 400 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS errors "
                         "FROM app_events WHERE ts >= ? AND kind IN ('access','s2s')", (since_ms,))[0]
        first_day = now_ms // DAY_MS - (days - 1)
        series: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
        for r in self._all("SELECT ts / ? AS day, event_type, COUNT(*) AS n FROM app_events WHERE ts >= ? AND "
                           "source = 'keycloak' AND event_type IN ('LOGIN','LOGIN_ERROR') GROUP BY 1, 2",
                           (DAY_MS, first_day * DAY_MS)):
            series.setdefault(int(r["day"]), {})[r["event_type"]] = int(r["n"])
        daily = []
        for day in range(first_day, first_day + days):
            counts = series.get(day, {})
            daily.append({"day_ms": day * DAY_MS, "logins": counts.get("LOGIN", 0),
                          "failed": counts.get("LOGIN_ERROR", 0)})
        active = self._one("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_sessions WHERE logout_at IS NULL AND last_seen_at >= ?",
                           (now_ms - idle_ms,))
        return {
            "total_logins": count(f"{kc} AND event_type = 'LOGIN'"),
            "failed_logins": count(f"{kc} AND event_type = 'LOGIN_ERROR'"),
            "app_logins": count("source = 'app' AND event_type = 'LOGIN'"),
            "token_refreshes": count("source = 'app' AND event_type = 'TOKEN_REFRESH'"),
            "expiry_warnings": count("event_type IN ('TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING','TOKEN_EXPIRED')"),
            "s2s_requests": count("kind = 's2s'"),
            "http_requests": int(http["n"] or 0),
            "http_errors": int(http["errors"] or 0),
            "avg_duration_ms": round(float(http["avg_ms"] or 0), 1),
            "active_sessions": int(active or 0),
            "top_users": top,
            "daily": daily,
        }

logapp/event_sync.py - 109 lines, extracted from the repository at build time

"""Pull Keycloak's own event log (logins, failures, logouts, token refreshes) into the dashboard database.

Keycloak stores events in ``event_entity`` and exposes them at ``GET /admin/realms/<realm>/events``.
Each event gets a content hash (``dedupe_key``) instead of relying on Keycloak's event id: syncing the same window
twice never creates duplicates, which also makes it safe to run in several gunicorn workers.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import requests

from store import Store, dedupe_key

log = logging.getLogger("logapp.sync")

PAGE = 200            # events requested per HTTP call
MAX_PAGES = 25        # safety valve: at most 5000 events per sync run
STATE_KEY = "keycloak_events_watermark_ms"


def normalize(raw: dict, store: Store) -> dict:
    """Map one Keycloak event JSON object to ``Store.add_event`` keyword arguments."""
    details = raw.get("details") or {}
    user_id = raw.get("userId")
    username = details.get("username") or (store.username_for_user_id(user_id) if user_id else None)
    if not username and raw.get("type", "").startswith("CLIENT_LOGIN") and raw.get("clientId"):
        username = f"service-account-{raw['clientId']}"
    extra = {k: v for k, v in details.items() if k != "username"}
    return {
        "ts": int(raw["time"]), "source": "keycloak", "kind": "auth",
        "event_type": raw.get("type", "UNKNOWN"), "username": username, "user_id": user_id,
        "client_id": raw.get("clientId"), "session_id": raw.get("sessionId"), "ip": raw.get("ipAddress"),
        "error": raw.get("error"), "detail": extra or None,
        "dedupe_key": dedupe_key("kc", raw.get("time"), raw.get("type"), user_id, raw.get("sessionId"),
                                 raw.get("clientId"), raw.get("ipAddress"), raw.get("error"),
                                 details.get("code_id"), details.get("username")),
    }


class KeycloakEventSync:
    """Incrementally copies Keycloak events into the store."""

    def __init__(self, store: Store, tokens, admin_api_base: str, http=requests, interval: int = 10):
        self.store, self.tokens, self.base, self._http, self.interval = store, tokens, admin_api_base, http, interval
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None
        self.last_error: str | None = None
        self.last_run_ms: int | None = None

    def _fetch(self, date_from: str, first: int) -> list[dict]:
        resp = self._http.get(f"{self.base}/events", timeout=10,
                              params={"dateFrom": date_from, "first": first, "max": PAGE},
                              headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.tokens.token()}"})
        if resp.status_code == 401:
            self.tokens.invalidate()
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()

    def sync_once(self) -> int:
        """Fetch events at or after the watermark's day; returns how many new rows were stored."""
        watermark = int(self.store.get_state(STATE_KEY, "0") or 0)
        date_from = datetime.fromtimestamp(watermark / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        new, newest, first = 0, watermark, 0
        for _ in range(MAX_PAGES):
            batch = self._fetch(date_from, first)
            for raw in batch:
                if "time" not in raw:
                    continue
                if self.store.add_event(**normalize(raw, self.store)):
                    new += 1
                newest = max(newest, int(raw["time"]))
            if len(batch) < PAGE:
                break
            first += PAGE
        # The next run re-reads the whole UTC day of the watermark (the REST filter has day granularity);
        # the dedupe key makes that overlap harmless.
        self.store.set_state(STATE_KEY, str(newest))
        return new

    def run_safely(self) -> int:
        try:
            n = self.sync_once()
            self.last_error = None
            return n
        except Exception as exc:  # Keycloak down or token refused: keep the app alive, report on the dashboard
            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            log.warning("keycloak event sync failed: %s", self.last_error)
            return 0
        finally:
            self.last_run_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)

    def start(self) -> None:
        if self._thread and self._thread.is_alive():
            return

        def loop():
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                self.run_safely()
                self._stop.wait(self.interval)

        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=loop, name="keycloak-event-sync", daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()

"""OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant with an in-memory token cache (service-to-service authentication)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import time

import requests


class TokenSource:
    """Hands out a valid access token for a machine identity, re-requesting it shortly before it expires.

    Used twice by the log app: with the ``demo-logapp`` identity to read Keycloak events (this needs the
    ``kc-admin-api`` scope: Keycloak 26.8 rejects Admin REST calls whose token lacks the admin API audience),
    and with the ``demo-service`` identity for the service-to-service probe against the demo API.
    """

    def __init__(self, token_url: str, client_id: str, client_secret: str, http=requests,
                 skew: int = 30, clock=time.time, scope: str | None = None):
        self.token_url, self.client_id, self._secret, self.scope = token_url, client_id, client_secret, scope
        self._http, self._skew, self._clock = http, skew, clock
        self._token: str | None = None
        self._expires_at = 0.0
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def token(self) -> str:
        with self._lock:
            if self._token is None or self._clock() >= self._expires_at - self._skew:
                data = {"grant_type": "client_credentials", "client_id": self.client_id,
                        "client_secret": self._secret}
                if self.scope:
                    data["scope"] = self.scope
                resp = self._http.post(self.token_url, timeout=10, data=data)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                body = resp.json()
                self._token = body["access_token"]
                self._expires_at = self._clock() + int(body.get("expires_in", 60))
            return self._token

    def invalidate(self) -> None:
        """Forget the cached token (e.g. after the resource server answered 401)."""
        with self._lock:
            self._token = None

"""Configuration of the log dashboard. Everything comes from environment variables (see ``.env.example``)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

REQUIRED = ("OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL", "OIDC_CLIENT_ID", "OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET", "LOGAPP_SESSION_SECRET",
            "LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL", "API_BASE_URL", "LOGAPP_DATABASE_URL", "SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET")


def _int(env, name: str, default: int, minimum: int = 1) -> int:
    raw = env.get(name)
    if raw in (None, ""):
        return default
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} must be an integer, got {raw!r}") from None
    if value < minimum:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} must be >= {minimum}, got {value}")
    return value


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    discovery_url: str
    client_id: str
    client_secret: str
    session_secret: str
    public_url: str
    api_base_url: str
    database_url: str
    service_client_id: str
    service_client_secret: str
    admin_role: str = "app-admin"
    sync_interval: int = 10        # seconds between Keycloak event pulls
    expiry_warn: int = 60          # warn when the access token has this many seconds left
    page_size: int = 25            # rows per dashboard page
    idle_minutes: int = 30         # a session unseen for this long is not "active"
    trust_proxy: bool = False      # honour X-Forwarded-* from the reverse proxy (online deployment)

    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls, env) -> "Config":
        missing = [k for k in REQUIRED if not env.get(k)]
        if missing:
            raise RuntimeError(f"missing environment variables: {', '.join(missing)}")
        return cls(
            discovery_url=env["OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL"],
            client_id=env["OIDC_CLIENT_ID"],
            client_secret=env["OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET"],
            session_secret=env["LOGAPP_SESSION_SECRET"],
            public_url=env["LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL"].rstrip("/"),
            api_base_url=env["API_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/"),
            database_url=env["LOGAPP_DATABASE_URL"],
            service_client_id=env.get("SERVICE_CLIENT_ID") or "demo-service",
            service_client_secret=env["SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET"],
            admin_role=env.get("LOGAPP_ADMIN_ROLE") or "app-admin",
            sync_interval=_int(env, "LOGAPP_SYNC_INTERVAL", 10),
            expiry_warn=_int(env, "LOGAPP_EXPIRY_WARN_SECONDS", 60),
            page_size=_int(env, "LOGAPP_PAGE_SIZE", 25),
            idle_minutes=_int(env, "LOGAPP_IDLE_MINUTES", 30),
            trust_proxy=str(env.get("LOGAPP_TRUST_PROXY", "")).lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"),
        )

    @property
    def realm(self) -> str:
        """Realm name parsed from the discovery URL ``.../realms/<realm>/.well-known/...``."""
        return self.discovery_url.split("/realms/", 1)[1].split("/", 1)[0]

    @property
    def token_url(self) -> str:
        """Token endpoint on the same (internal) host as the discovery URL."""
        return self.discovery_url.split("/.well-known/", 1)[0] + "/protocol/openid-connect/token"

    @property
    def admin_api_base(self) -> str:
        """Keycloak Admin REST base for the realm, on the same (internal) host as the discovery URL."""
        return f"{self.discovery_url.split('/realms/', 1)[0]}/admin/realms/{self.realm}"

    @property
    def secure_cookies(self) -> bool:
        return self.public_url.startswith("https://")

"""Pure helpers for the log dashboard (no Flask / network, easy to unit test)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import re
import time
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from urllib.parse import urlencode

DAY_MS = 86_400_000
STATUS_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{3}|\dxx)$", re.I)


def decode_jwt_payload(token: str | None) -> dict:
    """Decode a JWT payload **without verifying it** (display / expiry bookkeeping only).

    The token arrived over the back channel directly from Keycloak. Returns ``{}`` for anything malformed.
    """
    try:
        payload = token.split(".")[1]
        payload += "=" * (-len(payload) % 4)
        data = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload.encode()))
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
    except (IndexError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        return {}


def realm_roles(claims: dict) -> list[str]:
    hidden = {"offline_access", "uma_authorization"}
    roles = claims.get("realm_access", {}).get("roles", [])
    return sorted(r for r in roles if r not in hidden and not r.startswith("default-roles-"))


def seconds_left(exp: float | int | None, now: float | None = None) -> int:
    """Seconds until ``exp`` (never negative; 0 when unknown)."""
    if not isinstance(exp, (int, float)):
        return 0
    return max(0, int(exp - (time.time() if now is None else now)))


def build_logout_url(end_session_endpoint: str, id_token: str | None, post_logout_redirect_uri: str,
                     client_id: str) -> str:
    """RP-initiated logout URL (OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0)."""
    params = {"post_logout_redirect_uri": post_logout_redirect_uri, "client_id": client_id}
    if id_token:
        params["id_token_hint"] = id_token
    return f"{end_session_endpoint}?{urlencode(params)}"


def parse_day(value: str | None) -> date | None:
    """``YYYY-MM-DD`` -> date; ``None`` for empty or invalid input (a bad filter is ignored, not an error)."""
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value.strip()) if value and value.strip() else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


def day_start_ms(day: date) -> int:
    return int(datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)


def parse_filters(args, force_username: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Turn query-string arguments into a validated filter dict for ``Store.query_events``.

    ``force_username`` pins the user filter (non-admins may only see their own events). The end date is
    inclusive in the UI, therefore ``date_to`` is the start of the following day.
    """
    f: dict = {}
    f["username_exact"] = force_username or ""
    f["username"] = "" if force_username else (args.get("username") or "").strip()[:100]
    f["event_type"] = (args.get("event_type") or "").strip()[:60]
    f["kind"] = (args.get("kind") or "").strip()[:30]
    source = (args.get("source") or "").strip()
    f["source"] = source if source in ("app", "keycloak") else ""
    status = (args.get("status") or "").strip()
    f["status"] = status.lower() if STATUS_RE.match(status) else ""
    f["q"] = (args.get("q") or "").strip()[:100]
    start, end = parse_day(args.get("date_from")), parse_day(args.get("date_to"))
    f["date_from"] = day_start_ms(start) if start else None
    f["date_to"] = day_start_ms(end + timedelta(days=1)) if end else None
    return f


def page_number(args) -> int:
    try:
        return max(1, int(args.get("page", 1)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 1


def page_count(total: int, page_size: int) -> int:
    return max(1, -(-total // page_size))


def fmt_ts(ms: int | None) -> str:
    """Epoch milliseconds -> ``YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`` (UTC)."""
    if ms is None:
        return ""
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")


def fmt_day(ms: int) -> str:
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%a %d %b")


def severity(event_type: str, status: int | None) -> str:
    """CSS class for a log row: ``bad``, ``warn`` or ``ok``."""
    if event_type in ("LOGIN_ERROR", "CLIENT_LOGIN_ERROR", "TOKEN_EXPIRED", "TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED",
                      "S2S_ERROR", "ACCESS_DENIED") or (status is not None and status >= 500):
        return "bad"
    if event_type == "TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING" or (status is not None and status >= 400):
        return "warn"
    return "ok"

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Log dashboard (Flask + Authlib + psycopg). Valid as Dockerfile and Containerfile.

# ---- Build stage: resolve and install dependencies ----
FROM python:3.12-slim AS build
WORKDIR /build
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --prefix=/install -r requirements.txt

# ---- Runtime stage ----
FROM python:3.12-slim
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /install /usr/local
COPY log_app.py event_sync.py log_config.py log_helpers.py store.py token_source.py ./
COPY templates ./templates
COPY static ./static
# Run as an unprivileged user.
RUN useradd --system --no-create-home app && chown -R app /app
USER app
EXPOSE 8083
# One worker process: tokens live in process memory (see app.py). Concurrency comes from threads.
CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8083", "--no-control-socket", "--workers", "1", "--threads", "8", "--access-logfile", "-", "log_app:get_wsgi_app()"]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scripted browser session against the log dashboard (used by scripts/verify.sh).

Logs in through the real Keycloak login form, exercises the dashboard and prints ``PASS``/``FAIL`` lines.
Environment: LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL, KC_HOSTNAME, DEMO_REALM, DEMO_USER_PASSWORD, DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD, VERIFY_INSECURE.
Exit code 0 = every check passed. Needs only the standard library plus ``requests``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import sys
import time
from html import unescape

import requests

FAILED = 0


def check(ok: bool, text: str) -> None:
    global FAILED
    print(("PASS  " if ok else "FAIL  ") + text)
    FAILED += 0 if ok else 1


def _treat_localhost_as_secure(session: requests.Session, base: str) -> None:
    """Browsers send ``Secure`` cookies to http://localhost; ``requests`` does not, so mimic the browser."""
    if base.startswith("http://"):
        for cookie in session.cookies:
            cookie.secure = False


def sign_in(base: str, username: str, password: str, verify: bool) -> requests.Session:
    """Follow /login -> Keycloak form -> /callback and return the authenticated session."""
    s = requests.Session()
    s.verify = verify
    page = s.get(f"{base}/login", timeout=20)
    _treat_localhost_as_secure(s, base)
    m = re.search(r'<form[^>]*id="kc-form-login"[^>]*action="([^"]+)"', page.text) or \
        re.search(r'<form[^>]*action="([^"]+)"[^>]*id="kc-form-login"', page.text)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no Keycloak login form found (landed on {page.url})")
    resp = s.post(unescape(m.group(1)), data={"username": username, "password": password}, timeout=20)
    if not resp.url.startswith(base):
        raise RuntimeError(f"login of {username} failed (landed on {resp.url})")
    return s


def csrf_of(session: requests.Session, base: str) -> str:
    html = session.get(f"{base}/dashboard", timeout=20).text
    return re.search(r'name="csrf" value="([^"]+)"', html).group(1)


def events(session: requests.Session, base: str, **params) -> list[dict]:
    return session.get(f"{base}/events.json", params=params, timeout=20).json()["events"]


def main() -> int:
    base = os.environ.get("LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL", "http://localhost:8083").rstrip("/")
    verify = not os.environ.get("VERIFY_INSECURE")
    alice_pw, bob_pw = os.environ.get("DEMO_USER_PASSWORD", ""), os.environ.get("DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD", "")
    print(f"== Log dashboard ({base})")

    check(requests.get(f"{base}/healthz", timeout=15, verify=verify).json().get("database") is True,
          "health endpoint reports the database")
    anon = requests.get(f"{base}/dashboard", allow_redirects=False, timeout=15, verify=verify)
    check(anon.status_code == 302 and anon.headers["Location"].endswith("/login"), "anonymous users are sent to login")

    try:
        alice = sign_in(base, "alice", alice_pw, verify)
        bob = sign_in(base, "bob", bob_pw, verify)
    except Exception as exc:  # wrong passwords, Keycloak down ...
        check(False, f"login through Keycloak ({exc})")
        return 1
    check("Signed in as <b>alice</b>" in alice.get(f"{base}/dashboard", timeout=20).text, "alice signs in with Authorization Code + PKCE")

    # Drive some traffic: allowed and denied API calls plus a service-to-service call.
    token = csrf_of(bob, base)
    for key in ("me", "reports", "admin"):
        bob.post(f"{base}/api-call/{key}", data={"csrf": token}, timeout=30)
    bob.post(f"{base}/s2s", data={"csrf": token}, timeout=30)
    atoken = csrf_of(alice, base)
    alice.post(f"{base}/api-call/admin", data={"csrf": atoken}, timeout=30)   # alice may not -> 403

    api = {(e["username"], e["path"]): e["status"] for e in events(bob, base, kind="api")}
    check(api.get(("bob", "/api/admin")) == 200 and api.get(("alice", "/api/admin")) == 403,
          "API calls are logged with method, path and status (bob 200, alice 403)")
    check(all(e["duration_ms"] is not None for e in events(bob, base, kind="api")), "API calls record their duration")
    s2s = events(bob, base, kind="s2s")
    check(bool(s2s) and s2s[0]["username"] == "service-account-demo-service" and s2s[0]["status"] == 200,
          "service-to-service request is logged as the demo-service identity")
    check("LOGIN" in {e["event_type"] for e in events(bob, base, source="app")}, "application login events are logged")
    check(any(e["method"] == "GET" and e["path"] == "/dashboard" for e in events(bob, base, kind="access")),
          "HTTP access log has method, path and status")

    # Keycloak's own events arrive through the background sync (interval 10 s by default).
    deadline = time.time() + 45
    kc = []
    while time.time() < deadline:
        kc = events(bob, base, source="keycloak", event_type="LOGIN")
        if {"alice", "bob"} <= {e["username"] for e in kc}:
            break
        time.sleep(3)
    check({"alice", "bob"} <= {e["username"] for e in kc}, "Keycloak LOGIN events are synchronised (admin REST, view-events)")

    # Filters.
    check({e["username"] for e in events(bob, base, username="ali")} == {"alice"}, "admin filter by username")
    today = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.gmtime())
    check(len(events(bob, base, date_from=today, date_to=today)) > 0, "filter by date range")
    check(len(events(bob, base, date_from="2000-01-01", date_to="2000-01-02")) == 0, "date range without events is empty")
    check(all(e["status"] == 403 for e in events(bob, base, status="403")) and events(bob, base, status="403"),
          "filter by status code")
    check(all(400 <= e["status"] < 500 for e in events(bob, base, status="4xx")), "filter by status class (4xx)")
    check(len(events(bob, base, event_type="API_CALL")) > 0, "filter by event type")

    # Authorization inside the dashboard.
    check({e["username"] for e in events(alice, base, username="bob")} <= {"alice"},
          "non-admin cannot read other users' events (username filter is pinned)")
    check(alice.get(f"{base}/admin", timeout=20).status_code == 403, "admin panel is forbidden for alice")
    panel = bob.get(f"{base}/admin", timeout=20)
    check(panel.status_code == 200 and "Most active users" in panel.text and "Failed attempts" in panel.text,
          "admin panel shows aggregate statistics for bob")
    check("ACCESS_DENIED" in {e["event_type"] for e in events(bob, base, event_type="ACCESS_DENIED")}, "denied admin access is logged")

    # Logout is logged and ends the session.
    alice.get(f"{base}/logout", timeout=20)
    check(alice.get(f"{base}/dashboard", allow_redirects=False, timeout=20).status_code == 302, "logout ends the session")
    check("LOGOUT" in {e["event_type"] for e in events(bob, base, event_type="LOGOUT")}, "logout event is logged")

    print()
    print("LOGAPP VERIFY OK" if FAILED == 0 else "LOGAPP VERIFY FAILED")
    return 1 if FAILED else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

JSON schemas and API contracts

There is no dashboard /api contract. The JSON endpoints of the dashboard are /events.json (login required, same filters as the page) and /healthz ({"status":"UP","database":true}, 503 when the database is down). The /api/* routes belong to the separate api service.

Token refresh flow

Refresh flow: enforce_token_lifecycle checks the access token before every request. With fewer than LOGAPP_EXPIRY_WARN_SECONDS left it logs TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING, posts grant_type=refresh_token to the token endpoint and logs TOKEN_REFRESH (or TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED). Keycloak independently records REFRESH_TOKEN, which the sync imports. See logapp/log_app.py:107.
