Deployment procedures (full Docs/Deployment.md)

Docs/Deployment.md

Online deployment

The same containers run online. The overlay docker-compose.prod.yml adds Caddy, which obtains and renews Let's Encrypt certificates automatically and forwards traffic to Keycloak, the web app, the API and the log dashboard.

Rendered as source: no static drawing is bundled for this diagram.

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
    Internet((Internet)) -->|443 / 80| Caddy
    subgraph Server["Single VM (Docker or Podman)"]
        Caddy -->|auth.example.com| KC[Keycloak :8080]
        Caddy -->|app.example.com| Web[Web app :8081]
        Caddy -->|api.example.com| API[API :8082]
        Caddy -->|logs.example.com| Log[Log dashboard :8083]
        KC --> PG[(PostgreSQL volume)]
        Web --> KC
        API --> KC
        Log --> KC
        Log --> PG
        Log --> API
    end

Only ports 80 and 443 are published to the internet. The service ports stay bound to 127.0.0.1 (BIND_ADDRESS).

Status: the production overlay was exercised end to end on a developer machine by simulating the online setup with https://auth.localhost, app.localhost and api.localhost (done before the log dashboard and its logs.localhost host were added; repeat it with four names before relying on the dashboard online) (Caddy issues certificates from its internal CA for .localhost names). Verified: HTTPS everywhere, HTTP to HTTPS redirect, HSTS header, token issuer https://auth.localhost/realms/demo, VERIFY_CURL_OPTS=-k scripts/verify.sh = VERIFY OK, and /admin plus the master realm answering 403 outside ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDR. Not testable without a public server: the Let's Encrypt (ACME) issuance itself. It needs DNS pointing at the server and ports 80/443 reachable; step 7 shows how to confirm it. You can repeat the simulation: set the *_PUBLIC_*/*_HOSTNAME values to the .localhost names, run scripts/start.sh --prod, then VERIFY_CURL_OPTS=-k scripts/verify.sh.

Option A - any Linux VM (recommended path)

Works on any provider that gives you a VM with a public IP (IBM Cloud VSI, AWS EC2, Azure VM, GCP Compute Engine, Hetzner, DigitalOcean, ...). Sizing: 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM minimum for this demo (Keycloak needs about 1 GB heap headroom).

1. Provision the server
  • Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (or similar), public IPv4, inbound firewall rules: 22 (restrict to your IP), 80, 443.
  • Do not open 8080, 8081, 8082 or 8083.
2. Install a container engine
# Docker (Ubuntu)
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh && sudo usermod -aG docker $USER && newgrp docker
docker compose version

(Podman works too: sudo apt install podman docker-compose; set COMPOSE_CMD="podman compose". Rootless Podman cannot bind ports 80/443 without sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80.)

3. DNS names

Create four A records pointing at the server IP (or one wildcard):

auth.example.com   A  <server-ip>
app.example.com    A  <server-ip>
api.example.com    A  <server-ip>
logs.example.com   A  <server-ip>

No domain? Use sslip.io: for IP 203.0.113.10 the names auth.203-0-113-10.sslip.io, app.203-0-113-10.sslip.io, api.203-0-113-10.sslip.io and logs.203-0-113-10.sslip.io resolve automatically.

4. Get the code and configure
git clone <this repository> keycloak-implementation && cd keycloak-implementation
scripts/init-env.sh        # random secrets
nano .env                  # edit the values below

Set in .env (replace example.com by your domain):

KC_PUBLIC_HOST=auth.example.com
APP_PUBLIC_HOST=app.example.com
API_PUBLIC_HOST=api.example.com
LOGAPP_PUBLIC_HOST=logs.example.com
ACME_EMAIL=you@yourdomain.tld

KC_HOSTNAME=https://auth.example.com
WEBAPP_PUBLIC_URL=https://app.example.com
API_PUBLIC_URL=https://api.example.com
LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL=https://logs.example.com
BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1

# demo hardening - see the checklist below
DEMO_REGISTRATION_ALLOWED=false
DEMO_CLI_ENABLED=true         # keep true only until step 7 is done, then set false and re-import (see checklist)
ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDR="203.0.113.0/24"   # your office/VPN range; keep "0.0.0.0/0 ::/0" only while testing
5. Start
scripts/start.sh --prod

This builds the images and starts PostgreSQL, Keycloak, the API, the web app, the log dashboard and Caddy. The readiness loop in start.sh checks 127.0.0.1, so it works behind the proxy. Caddy requests the certificates on first contact (allow a minute; watch docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f caddy).

6. First login to the admin console

https://auth.example.com/admin with KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME and the password from .env. Create a permanent admin user with a strong password and MFA, then delete the bootstrap admin (Keycloak shows a banner reminding you).

7. Verify the deployment

From your laptop (any machine with curl and the .env values; copy only the variables needed):

# a) certificates and discovery
curl -sI https://auth.example.com/realms/demo/.well-known/openid-configuration | head -1     # HTTP/2 200
curl -s  https://auth.example.com/realms/demo/.well-known/openid-configuration | python3 -m json.tool | grep '"issuer"'
#    -> "issuer": "https://auth.example.com/realms/demo"     (must be https and your public host)

# b) full end-to-end check (uses the public URLs from .env)
scripts/verify.sh                                           # expected: VERIFY OK (add VERIFY_CURL_OPTS=-k only for self-signed tests)

# c) browser test
#    open https://app.example.com -> Sign in -> alice or bob -> try the four API buttons
#    alice: reports 200, write/admin 403.  bob: all allowed.

#    open https://logs.example.com -> sign in as bob -> events, filters, Admin page statistics

# d) negative checks
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.example.com/api/reports                  # 401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://logs.example.com/dashboard                      # 302 (anonymous users are sent to /login)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://app.example.com                               # 308 redirect to https
# from an address outside ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDR:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://auth.example.com/admin/                      # 403

Run scripts/verify.sh on the server itself too: it reads the same .env, so it tests the public HTTPS URLs.

8. Operate
Task Command (append -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml or export MODE=prod for scripts)
Logs docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f
Update the stack git pull && scripts/start.sh --prod
Upgrade Keycloak change KEYCLOAK_VERSION, scripts/start.sh --prod (back up first)
Stop scripts/stop.sh --prod
Database backup (includes the logapp schema) docker compose exec postgres pg_dump -U $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB > backup-$(date +%F).sql
Restore docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB < backup.sql
Destroy everything scripts/stop.sh --prod --volumes (deletes the database)

Option B - other platforms

The four application images are standard OCI images, so any container service can run them. What each platform must provide is the same:

Requirement Detail
Keycloak container Build keycloak/Dockerfile; start command start --optimized --import-realm (already the image default). Needs KC_DB_URL, KC_DB_USERNAME, KC_DB_PASSWORD, KC_HOSTNAME (public https URL), KC_HTTP_ENABLED=true, KC_PROXY_HEADERS=xforwarded (or forwarded) when TLS is terminated by the platform, the bootstrap admin variables and the realm placeholder variables
Database Managed PostgreSQL 15+ (the image is built with KC_DB=postgres)
TLS Terminated by the platform load balancer; Keycloak must see X-Forwarded-Proto/Host
Health probe GET :9000/health/ready (management port; do not expose it publicly)
Back channel The API and web app need to reach Keycloak. Point OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL to the internal address when available, otherwise to KC_HOSTNAME; OIDC_ISSUER must always equal the public issuer. KC_HOSTNAME_BACKCHANNEL_DYNAMIC=true is only needed when the internal address differs from KC_HOSTNAME
Web app and API One instance each, env vars as in docker-compose.yml; WEBAPP_PUBLIC_URL must be the public https URL
Log dashboard Exactly one always-on instance (tokens live in its memory, the event sync is a background thread; scale-to-zero stops the sync and signs users out). Needs LOGAPP_DATABASE_URL, LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL, LOGAPP_SESSION_SECRET, OIDC_*, API_BASE_URL, SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET
Persistence Only the database holds state; the web app and API are stateless (the web app keeps the session in a signed cookie); the log dashboard keeps only tokens in memory and everything else in PostgreSQL

Typical mappings (not exercised in this project; follow the provider's current documentation for exact commands):

Platform Mapping
IBM Cloud Code Engine / Google Cloud Run / Azure Container Apps Four container apps + managed PostgreSQL; platform provides HTTPS; set KC_PROXY_HEADERS=xforwarded and a minimum of one Keycloak instance (cold starts take ~20 s)
Kubernetes Deployments + Services for the four images, a managed PostgreSQL or an operator, an Ingress with TLS; for production prefer the official Keycloak Operator
Render / Railway / Fly.io Docker services from the four Dockerfiles + managed PostgreSQL; use the platform's HTTPS domain for KC_HOSTNAME

Hardening checklist

Complete before exposing real users:

  • [ ] DEMO_REGISTRATION_ALLOWED=false (or add e-mail verification with SMTP).
  • [ ] Set DEMO_CLI_ENABLED=false: it enables the password grant. Because the realm is imported only once, apply it on an existing deployment in the admin console (Clients > demo-cli > disable) or wipe and re-import.
  • [ ] Keep the log dashboard behind HTTPS only (LOGAPP_TRUST_PROXY=true is set by the prod overlay); it stores IPs and usernames in the logapp schema, so define a retention policy (see Retention SQL) and back it up with the database.
  • [ ] Rotate LOGAPP_CLIENT_SECRET and LOGAPP_SESSION_SECRET (admin console: Clients > demo-logapp > Credentials; rotating the session secret signs everybody out).
  • [ ] Rotate SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET (admin console: Clients > demo-service > Credentials) and store it in your secret manager; give real services their own clients instead of sharing demo-service.
  • [ ] Delete or re-password the demo users alice and bob.
  • [ ] Replace the bootstrap admin by a named admin with MFA.
  • [ ] Restrict /admin and the master realm with ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDR, or serve the admin console only on a private network.
  • [ ] Configure SMTP (Realm settings > Email) and set verifyEmail / password reset flows.
  • [ ] Back up PostgreSQL on a schedule and test a restore.
  • [ ] Keep Keycloak, base images and Python dependencies current; subscribe to the Keycloak security advisories.
  • [ ] Use a managed or separately hardened PostgreSQL and rotate POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
  • [ ] Enable KC_LOG_LEVEL/metrics collection: the image already enables /metrics on the management port 9000 (not published).
Retention SQL

Every logapp timestamp is epoch milliseconds (BIGINT), so compare against extract(epoch ...) * 1000, not against now(). Run it from cron through compose exec postgres psql; the example keeps 90 days.

DELETE FROM logapp.app_events WHERE ts < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;
DELETE FROM logapp.audit_log WHERE ts < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;
DELETE FROM logapp.user_sessions WHERE logout_at IS NOT NULL AND login_at < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;

Troubleshooting (online)

Symptom Cause and fix
Browser certificate warning Certificate not yet issued or DNS wrong: logs caddy; ports 80/443 must be reachable from the internet; Let's Encrypt rate limits apply to repeated failures
"Invalid parameter: redirect_uri" WEBAPP_PUBLIC_URL differs from what was imported; wipe and re-import or edit client demo-webapp
Keycloak shows http:// links or loops on login Proxy headers not trusted: confirm KC_PROXY_HEADERS=xforwarded (prod overlay) and that you started with --prod
API 401 for valid tokens KC_HOSTNAME must be exactly the issuer host used to obtain the token (scheme, host, no trailing slash)
verify.sh fails at the service token step SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET in .env differs from the imported one (realm imported before the variable existed: wipe and re-import, or set the secret in the admin console)
verify.sh fails at token step DEMO_CLI_ENABLED=false, or .env passwords differ from the imported ones
Dashboard shows no Keycloak events online LOGAPP_CLIENT_SECRET differs from the imported one (wipe and re-import or set it in Clients > demo-logapp > Credentials); check the Admin page for the last sync error
Login on the dashboard fails with invalid_scope The realm was imported with an older demo-logapp definition: the client must list its default scopes explicitly next to the optional kc-admin-api scope. Wipe and re-import or fix the client scopes in the admin console
Dashboard Admin page shows an event sync error mentioning 401 Keycloak 26.8 needs the audience <host>/admin/realms/<realm> on Admin REST tokens: check that client demo-logapp has the optional scope kc-admin-api and the service account has view-events (code: logapp/log_app.py ADMIN_API_SCOPE)

Retention SQL

Extracted from Docs/Deployment.md. ts, login_at and logout_at are epoch milliseconds. The earlier statement compared them with now() and failed on PostgreSQL; the version below was dry-run on the live database inside a transaction that was rolled back.

DELETE FROM logapp.app_events WHERE ts < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;
DELETE FROM logapp.audit_log WHERE ts < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;
DELETE FROM logapp.user_sessions WHERE logout_at IS NOT NULL AND login_at < (extract(epoch FROM now() - interval '90 days') * 1000)::bigint;

Glossary of terms, variables and parameters

Terms

TermMeaning
RealmKeycloak's isolated namespace of users, clients and roles. This project uses the realm demo.
ClientAn application registered in Keycloak: demo-webapp, demo-api, demo-logapp, demo-service, demo-cli.
OIDC / PKCEOpenID Connect authorization code flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange, used by the dashboard login.
Access tokenShort-lived (about 5 minutes) bearer token for the API. Kept only in the TokenVault.
Refresh tokenLong-lived token exchanged for a new access token (grant_type=refresh_token).
TokenVaultIn-process dictionary in log_app.py that holds the tokens by opaque session id; never persisted.
source=app / source=keycloakWhich writer produced an event row: this application's hooks or the Keycloak sync.
kindEvent category: auth, access, token, api, s2s.
dedupe_keyContent hash that makes re-reading overlapping Keycloak event windows idempotent.
watermarksync_state row keycloak_events_watermark_ms: how far the sync has read.
enabledEventTypesRealm setting listing the event types Keycloak stores; REFRESH_TOKEN is not stored by default.
kc-admin-apiOptional client scope that adds the Admin REST audience Keycloak 26.8 requires.
view-eventsRealm-management role of the dashboard's service account; the only admin permission it holds.
s2sService-to-service: the dashboard calls the api as demo-service with the client credentials grant.
app-user / app-adminRealm roles: app-admin sees all events and the admin page.
epoch millisecondsUnit of every timestamp in the logapp schema (BIGINT), the same unit Keycloak uses.

Environment variables of the dashboard

VariableMeaningRead in
OIDC_DISCOVERY_URLOIDC discovery document of the realm, on the internal Keycloak host; the token and admin REST URLs are derived from it (there is no separate internal-URL variable).logapp/log_config.py:6
OIDC_CLIENT_IDClient id of the dashboard in Keycloak (demo-logapp).logapp/log_config.py:6
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRETSecret of that client; compose passes LOGAPP_CLIENT_SECRET.logapp/log_config.py:6
LOGAPP_SESSION_SECRETSigns the dashboard's session cookie. .env.example default: changeme-logapp-session-secretlogapp/log_config.py:6
LOGAPP_PUBLIC_URLPublic URL of the dashboard; must match the redirect URI registered in Keycloak. .env.example default: http://localhost:8083logapp/log_config.py:7
API_BASE_URLBase URL of the api service used by the API buttons and the service-to-service call.logapp/log_config.py:7
LOGAPP_DATABASE_URLPostgreSQL connection URL of the dashboard (not DATABASE_URL). A sqlite: URL is used by tests.logapp/log_config.py:7
SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRETSecret of that client (client credentials grant). .env.example default: changeme-service-secretlogapp/log_config.py:7
SERVICE_CLIENT_IDClient id for the service-to-service call (default demo-service).logapp/log_config.py:54
LOGAPP_ADMIN_ROLERealm role that may open the admin page and see every user's events (default app-admin). .env.example default: app-adminlogapp/log_config.py:56
LOGAPP_SYNC_INTERVALSeconds between pulls of Keycloak's event log (default 10). .env.example default: 10logapp/log_config.py:57
LOGAPP_EXPIRY_WARN_SECONDSSeconds before access-token expiry at which TOKEN_EXPIRY_WARNING is logged and the refresh token is used (default 60). .env.example default: 60logapp/log_config.py:58
LOGAPP_PAGE_SIZERows per dashboard page (default 25). .env.example default: 25logapp/log_config.py:59
LOGAPP_IDLE_MINUTESA session unseen for this long no longer counts as active (default 30).logapp/log_config.py:60
LOGAPP_TRUST_PROXYHonour X-Forwarded-* headers of the reverse proxy; set by the prod overlay. .env.example default: falselogapp/log_config.py:61

Query parameters of /dashboard and /events.json

ParameterMeaning
usernameAdmin only. Substring match; for non-admins the filter is pinned to the signed-in user.
event_typeExact event type, e.g. LOGIN, API_CALL, REFRESH_TOKEN.
kindCategory: auth, access, token, api or s2s.
sourceOrigin: app (written by this application) or keycloak (pulled from the events REST endpoint).
statusHTTP status: an exact code such as 403, or a class such as 4xx.
qFree text over path and error.
date_fromFirst day (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, UTC.
date_toLast day (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, UTC.
page1-based page number.
livelive=1 adds a page-level meta refresh every 5 seconds (dashboard only, not /events.json).

Event kinds: auth, access, token, api, s2s.

Troubleshooting cross-referenced to code

Each code reference is resolved to a line number at build time, so a moved or deleted symbol breaks the build instead of leaving a dead link. More symptoms: Docs/Quickstart.md and Docs/Deployment.md.

SymptomCause and fixCode path
After a restart the dashboard asks me to sign in againBy design: tokens live in process memory, so open sessions are closed with the reason server_restart.logapp/log_app.py:141 logapp/log_app.py:49
No source=keycloak rowsThe sync needs the kc-admin-api scope and the view-events role; the Admin page shows the last sync error.logapp/event_sync.py:63 logapp/token_source.py:10 logapp/log_app.py:43
Event sync error mentioning 401Keycloak 26.8 rejects Admin REST tokens without the audience <host>/admin/realms/<realm>; check the optional scope.logapp/token_source.py:26 keycloak/realm/demo-realm.json:225
REFRESH_TOKEN rows never appearKeycloak does not store that type by default; it must be in enabledEventTypes (it is, in the demo realm).keycloak/realm/demo-realm.json:28
A refresh failed but I am still signed inTOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED is logged; the session ends with TOKEN_EXPIRED only when the access token really expired.logapp/log_app.py:5 logapp/log_app.py:5
403 on the admin pageOnly the role app-admin may open it; the attempt is logged as ACCESS_DENIED and written to audit_log.logapp/log_app.py:193 logapp/log_app.py:200
Dashboard returns 503 on /healthzThe database ping failed: check LOGAPP_DATABASE_URL and the postgres container.logapp/log_app.py:273 logapp/store.py:117
Container exits with 'missing environment variables'One of the required variables is unset; the message lists them.logapp/log_config.py:6 logapp/log_config.py:45
Invalid parameter: redirect_uriLOGAPP_PUBLIC_URL changed after the realm was imported: re-import or edit the client demo-logapp.logapp/log_config.py:51
Active sessions looks too highSessions stay active until logout or LOGAPP_IDLE_MINUTES without a request; verify.sh never signs bob out.logapp/store.py:253 logapp/log_config.py:38
Duplicate Keycloak rowsThey cannot occur: the unique dedupe_key plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING absorbs overlapping windows.logapp/store.py:137 logapp/store.py:49
Retention statement fails with 'operator does not exist: bigint'ts is epoch milliseconds; convert with extract(epoch FROM ...) * 1000 as in the Retention SQL section.logapp/store.py:28
